definitions.explanation: A large piece of cloth hung as a screen or divider, including stage curtains in theaters and decorative curtains used at events and ceremonies.

definitions.gloss: act (of a play or drama), scene
definitions.explanation: A division of a theatrical performance. Also used figuratively to describe a phase or chapter of events.

examples.japanese: {舞台|ぶたい}の{幕|まく}がゆっくりと{下|お}りた。
examples.english: The stage curtain slowly came down.

examples.japanese: お{祝|いわ}いの{席|せき}に{紅白|こうはく}の{幕|まく}が{張|は}られていた。
examples.english: Red and white curtains were hung at the celebration.

examples.japanese: {第|だい}{二|に}{幕|まく}が{始|はじ}まった。
{長|なが}い{戦争|せんそう}にようやく{幕|まく}が{下|お}りた。
examples.english: The long war finally came to an end.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{時代|じだい}の{幕開|まくあ}けを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: I feel the dawn of a new era.

notes:
USAGE:
Appears in many set expressions related to beginnings and endings. In kabuki and traditional theater, {幕|まく} is a fundamental structural unit. Also an important element in compounds related to the Edo period ({幕府|ばくふ} = shogunate, {幕末|ばくまつ} = end of Edo period).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる: the curtain rises (something begins)
- {幕|まく}が{下|お}りる: the curtain falls (something ends)
- {幕|まく}を{開|あ}ける: to open the curtain (to start)
- {幕開|まくあ}け: opening, beginning
- {幕|まく}{引|び}き: closing, wrapping up

RELATED COMPOUNDS:
- {幕府|ばくふ}: shogunate
- {幕末|ばくまつ}: end of the Edo period
- {幕内|まくうち}: top division (sumo); bento box
